subject: Performance SLO / VPC qualification follow-up - Acme Corp
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO / VPC qualification follow-up - Acme Corp

Hi Alex — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and next steps so we can size the private deployment and confirm the latency SLOs: 

1) Target latency: 95th percentile <= 120ms for short text generation (<=256 tokens). You mentioned internal budget is 150ms but you'd prefer to land at 120ms if possible.
2) Throughput/concurrency: initial target 200 concurrent requests, average 60 qps sustained, burst to 300 qps.
3) Streaming: client-side streaming required for partial token delivery for chat UX.
4) Network topology: you have a VPC in us-west-2 with a dedicated transit gateway and an existing VPN to your on-prem colo. Need egress rules and peering details to estimate RTT.

Attachments: I attached a short SLO worksheet (slo_requirements.xlsx) and a draft network diagram we sketched (network-diagram.pdf).

Next steps (proposed):
- You share traceroutes or internal latency samples and an updated network diagram (action: Acme SRE).
- We run a lightweight network qualification (TCP pings, MTU, and a few test streams) from your VPC to our private endpoint — needs a short maintenance window (~30m). (action: Redwood + Acme SRE)
- Redwood to provide a sizing and latency risk matrix by Monday (action: Jordan/Marissa).

If that all sounds right, can we lock a slot for the network run next week?

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmecorp.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: SRE Team <sre@acmecorp.com>, Procurement <procurement@acmecorp.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 16:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO / VPC qualification follow-up - Acme Corp

Jordan — thanks for the thorough recap. Confirming a few items from our side: 

- 95p target 120ms is aggressive but aligns with product goals; SRE flagged that our current internal median for similar endpoints is ~80ms, so 120ms end-to-end seems feasible with direct peering.
- Concurrency/throughput numbers look correct. We'll start with the 200 concurrent baseline.
- Streaming is required; our chat client expects token-level chunks.

I'll share the current network diagram and traceroutes by tomorrow EOD. For the network run, Thursday 2027-04-29 09:00 PT works for us — would that slot work for Redwood?

Also looping in Procurement for any NDAs / data transfer paperwork needed.

—Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Product Engineering, Acme Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmecorp.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO / VPC qualification follow-up - Acme Corp

Alex — great, thanks. A couple of clarifying network questions SRE asked while we were reviewing your diagram draft: 

1) Can you confirm whether the VPN is routed to the transit gateway or direct to the individual VPCs? If via TGW, what is the observed avg RTT from your app subnet to the TGW?
2) Do you have any NAT/egress proxies that might add extra hops or connection pooling that could affect TLS session reuse?
3) For streaming: are you okay with HTTP/2 chunked responses or do you need a raw TCP socket? Our streaming uses HTTP/2 by default but we can support alternative transports in private deployments.

If you can paste a short traceroute (3-5 hops) from one of your app nodes to our proposed endpoint and any firewall egress rules, that will help us estimate RTT contribution and failure modes.

I'll start the sizing write-up and include a latency risk table (network vs. queuing vs. CPU/GPUs). Jordan and I will align on the recommended instance shapes.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

From: SRE Team <sre@acmecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 11:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO / VPC qualification follow-up - Acme Corp

Marissa / Jordan — quick answers from SRE: 

- VPN terminates on the transit gateway (TGW). Avg RTT from app subnet to TGW is ~2.5ms.
- We do NAT egress via a fleet of proxy instances that perform TLS termination for legacy services; however, the new chat stack is on a private route that bypasses the proxy and performs direct egress.
- Client prefers HTTP/2 streaming — we can do that.

Traceroute (app-node-12 -> redwood-private-usw2):
  1  10.0.0.1 (10.0.0.1)  0.345 ms  0.289 ms  0.279 ms
  2  192.168.100.1 (192.168.100.1)  1.102 ms  1.099 ms  1.098 ms
  3  54.239.xx.xx (54.239.xx.xx)  6.233 ms  6.210 ms  6.195 ms

Firewall: allow outbound 443 to 54.239.XX.XX/32; keep-alive allowed.

We can schedule the network qualification on Thu 2027-04-29 09:00 PT. Please provide the exact test host/IP and the short maintenance window plan.

—Acme SRE

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmecorp.com>, SRE Team <sre@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 24 Apr 2027 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO / VPC qualification follow-up - Acme Corp

Perfect — thanks for the traceroute and confirmation. Action summary: 

- Network run confirmed Thu 2027-04-29 09:00 PT. Redwood will initiate TCP/HTTP/HTTP2 checks from redwood-private-usw2 (54.239.XX.XX).
- Acme SRE to open outbound 443 to 54.239.XX.XX/32 and provide a maintenance contact on the day.
- Marissa/Vivek to deliver sizing + latency risk matrix by Monday 2027-04-26.
- Jordan to produce a short test plan (30m window) and pre-shared test vectors for streaming.

I'll follow up with the test IP and a calendar invite. Looking forward to the run — if network looks good we can propose an initial dedicated pool config that meets the 95p 120ms target.

Thanks,
Jordan
